# EvBadge

> A badge is a small, color-coded label that communicates an item's status, category, or count using concise text.

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| ID | `evoq-ui:badge` |
| Layer | Atom (`src/atoms`) |
| Import | `import { EvBadge } from 'evoq-ui'` |
| Template tag | `<EvBadge>` or `<ev-badge>` |
| Source | `src/atoms/badge/EvBadge.vue` |
| Extra attributes go to | the root `<span class="ev-badge">` |


## Design guidance

From the Figma page **Badge**, frame `3804:28987` (Badge). These rules are binding. Names in them are Figma's - the Vue API is the tables above.

### When to use

- Use to communicate the status or state of an item (e.g., Success, Waiting, Reject).
- Use in tables, lists, or cards to label rows at a glance.
- Use the reverse (solid) style for high-emphasis or active states.
- Use the subtle style for low-emphasis, inline status.
- Use the Custom variant for domain-specific states not covered by the defaults.

### When not to use

- Don't use for interactive actions  →  use Button (`evoq-ui:button`)
- Don't use to identify a person  →  use Avatar (`evoq-ui:avatar`)
- Don't use for long text or full sentences  →  use plain text
- Don't use as a count bubble on an icon  →  use Notification dot (`evoq-ui:hint`)

### Do

- Keep labels to 1–2 words in title case
- Map each status to a consistent variant color
- Use the icon slot only when it adds meaning
- Pair color with text so meaning isn't color-only

### Don't

- Write full sentences inside a badge
- Reuse the same color for unrelated statuses
- Rely on color alone to convey meaning
- Stack multiple badges where one status suffices

## Contract

- Only the props, slots and events above exist on `EvBadge`; anything not listed is not part of its API.
- An attribute that is not a prop (`class`, `id`, `aria-*`, `data-*`) goes to the root `<span class="ev-badge">`.
- Import it by name from `evoq-ui`; styles come once from `evoq-ui/style.css`.
- Refer to it by id `evoq-ui:badge` - the id stays the same if the component moves layer.
